# Dating Algorithm — research review

Checked 2026-10-17. These notes accompany the unchanged Version B; they do not rewrite the essay or manufacture observations.

| Reference | Finding | Verification limit |
|---|---|---|
| Neyt, Vandenbulcke & Baert, 2019 | The published title and year are confirmed. The study used 24 experimental profiles, each liking 150 users: 3,600 evaluations. Education affected women's choices of male profiles more strongly; no evidence was reported that men avoided highly educated women. | Sample-specific app behaviour, not universal dating weights, human worth, or the author's missing N=10 data. |
| Buss, 1989 | The original paper reports 37 samples and 10,047 respondents, with average differences in stated preferences concerning resources and attractiveness. | Questionnaire findings about averages do not establish fixed 70%/90% coefficients or predict individuals. |
| Eastwick & Finkel, 2008 | The Northwestern author manuscript, publication record and abstract support the distinction between stated ideal preferences and attraction to actual speed-dating partners. | This does not establish that all preferences are useless or validate the essay's personal model. |
| Jiang Xueqin lecture | The original Predictive History video, title and 6 January 2026 date were located. | Exact five-by-five example and quoted equilibrium wording were not independently verified against primary video captions. The supplied link is a transcript mirror, not sufficient to close this item. |
| Trivers / Harari / historical examples | Attribution and broad context reviewed; no new scientific claim added to the reader. | No exact Sapiens passage or edition was supplied; these are not fully fact-checked quotations. |

Primary sources:

- [Neyt et al., IZA author working paper, sections 3.5 and 5](https://docs.iza.org/dp11933.pdf); [published article DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.econedurev.2019.101914). The 2018 working paper and 2019 journal version are distinct versions.
- [Buss, 1989, original paper hosted by the author's laboratory](https://labs.la.utexas.edu/buss/files/2015/10/buss-1989-sex-differences-in-human-mate-preferences.pdf).
- [Eastwick & Finkel, 2008, publication record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18211175/); [author publication page](https://elifinkel.com/publications-by-year/); [Northwestern author manuscript](https://faculty.wcas.northwestern.edu/eli-finkel/documents/MatePrefs_FINAL6-5-07_000.pdf).
- [Predictive History: Game Theory #1 — The Dating Game](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hE4l9WyLF3U).

The first paragraph is a narrator's model that the essay subsequently criticizes. The reader keeps the full sequence and its existing editorial context. Its preference control has no gender presets or people score. The new matching control illustrates assignments only, with no claim that equal ranks establish equilibrium. The invitation interaction leaves outcomes unknown.

The kit supplies no raw DOCX, participant logs, observations, identities, photos or consent records. The two supplied Markdown manuscripts are byte-identical. The data slot remains explicitly unfilled; the ten-row CSV and public table contain no results. Verification of actual N=10 research, detailed Jiang wording and the missing source document remains open.
